summary: OPS delivers the data, eventing, infrastructure and quality backbone every other domain stands on: indexed and RLS-forced Postgres with zero-downtime migrations, read models for the registry and owner reports, the transactional outbox relayed to Valkey Streams as PHI-free CloudEvents, Caffeine/Valkey caching with a PHI default-deny rule, SSE transport from core.realtime, OpenTelemetry/Prometheus/Grafana with SLO burn alerts and PHI-redacted logs, the CI pipeline and test suites (token misuse, concurrency, RBAC, tenant fuzzing, chaos, k6) with previews and release safety reports, phase gates, and per-country cells (India first, then UAE, KSA, Qatar) with backups, DR, KMS and egress proofs. It matters because the Phase 0 gate (no real patient data before it) and every Phase 1 'moment that matters' (live queue < 2 s, check-in < 300 ms, no duplicate WhatsApp) depend on it. 69 stories, 491.5 engineer-days. Tracker effort for the 72 in-scope tasks is 482 days; OPS covers 70 of them plus 7 Data & Infra / QA & CI squad tasks from other areas (501 tracker days), and cedes T-016 and T-095 (11 days) to FEF. The estimate is within about 2% of that: the 25-day items (T-094, T-096, T-255, T-272, T-290) were split into buildable stories, Playwright journeys and the WhatsApp provider stub are left to FEF and COM, and a 4-day Qatar readiness story with no tracker task was added.

stories.title: Patient timeline, registry and audit head load in milliseconds (missing indexes added, duplicates dropped)
stories.story: As a receptionist I want a patient's visit history and last visit to appear instantly so that I do not keep a patient waiting at the desk while the screen spins.
stories.context: DP-01/DP-25 measured a 2,485 ms cross-tenant sequential scan for every patient-scoped read of queue_entries, 5,041 ms for the audit chain head and a seq scan for the paediatric weight lookup (a safety path). Each index is created CONCURRENTLY in its own migration (Flyway runs a single-statement CONCURRENTLY migration non-transactionally) so the hot tables are never write-locked. Four indexes duplicate unique constraints and only add write cost; they are dropped. EXPLAIN plan-regression tests pin the plans so a later migration or policy change cannot silently regress them. Pairs with T-010 (indexable array RLS policy, Platform & Trust) which removes the OR-shaped policy that makes tenant_id non-indexable. Unblocks reception (registry, last visit), doctor (timeline, paediatric dose weight) and every audited write.

Given a tenant with no recent audit rows and 3M audit_log rows, when an audited write fires audit_log_chain(), then the head lookup takes < 1 ms (baseline 5,041 ms)
Given VitalsRepository.findLatestWeight for a child, when executed, then the plan is an Index Scan on the new partial vitals index (no Seq Scan)

Given a PR that changes a migration or repository SQL, when CI stage 3 runs, then the EXPLAIN regression suite fails if any pinned query loses its Index Cond on tenant_id

stories.title: Migrations follow an expand/contract playbook enforced by a CI migration lint, with a generated ERD
stories.story: As an engineer I want every migration checked against zero-downtime rules in CI so that a deploy during OPD hours never locks queue_entries or breaks the running pods.
stories.context: DP-12 found CREATE INDEX without CONCURRENTLY (V83, V43, V53, V60), CHECK swaps without NOT VALID on the hottest table (V5, V37, V39), full-table backfills inside the migration transaction followed by SET NOT NULL, destructive drops in the same release (V5, V39, V40) and version gaps (V49, V56-59, ...) with out-of-order disabled. The playbook (docs/architecture/migration-playbook.md) states the rules; a lint in CI stage 4 enforces them; versions are allocated centrally (next free number reserved in a VERSIONS file checked by CI) so parallel squads never collide. Backfills run as batched jobs that suppress set_updated_at (the cause of DP-13). The schema doc and ERD are generated from the catalog on every main build, replacing the PDF that covers 12 of 86 tables (DP-31). Unblocks every persona: zero-downtime deploys are the precondition for NFR-16 'updates never break a clinic day'.

stories.title: Tenant isolation is enforced by the database: split roles, FORCE RLS with per-command policies, timeouts and a prod-config CI job
stories.story: As a clinic owner (and DPO) I want the database itself to refuse cross-tenant access so that a single coding mistake can never show my patients to another clinic.
stories.context: MF-03: the app role runs Flyway and owns every table, so RLS is inert in deployment; no policy is FORCEd; seven tenant tables have no RLS and brand policies are USING-only (MF-63, QA-40). ADR-07 fixes this: nabd_migrator owns schemas and runs Flyway as a separate job, nabd_app is DML-only NOBYPASSRLS with statement_timeout=5s, lock_timeout=3s, idle_in_transaction_session_timeout=15s, nabd_reports is read-only with 60 s. Every tenant_id table gets FORCE RLS with per-command policies: USING tenant_id = ANY(app.visible_tenant_ids) and WITH CHECK tenant_id = app.tenant_id. The app refuses to boot if the invariant is broken, and a prod-config CI job migrates as nabd_migrator and runs the whole API suite as nabd_app. Hikari gets explicit settings (15-20 connections, 3 s connection timeout, leak detection 10 s) so pool exhaustion fails fast. Unblocks the Phase 0 exit gate (B-25 isolated tenant records) and every later story that relies on RLS.
acceptance: Given the app connects as nabd_app, when it boots, then RlsSelfCheck verifies via pg_class/pg_roles that nabd_app owns no RLS table, has no BYPASSRLS, and every table with a tenant_id column has relrowsecurity and relforcerowsecurity true, else startup fails with a named table list

Given Hikari is exhausted, when a request needs a connection, then it fails after 3 s with 503 instead of queueing 30 s
Given a PR, when the prod-config job runs (Flyway as nabd_migrator, API suite as nabd_app), then it passes and is a required check; scripts/dev-up.sh creates the same split roles locally

stories.title: Synced tables carry change_seq and updated_at so screens and apps can fetch only what changed
stories.story: As an engineer I want every table that a cache, SSE projection or app syncs to carry a monotonic change_seq so that ETags, SSE version gates and delta sync are possible.
stories.context: DP-19: 39 tables lack updated_at, including mutable invoices, prescriptions, procedure_orders, waitlist_entries and vitals, which blocks ETag/304, the SSE 'apply only if v > current' rule and the patient app's delta sync. A per-table change_seq from one sequence is assigned by a BEFORE INSERT OR UPDATE trigger with an index (tenant_id, change_seq). Same story: UUID v7 for new rows on append-heavy tables (DP-23), explicit column lists instead of SELECT * (DP-29), = ANY(?) batching for the small N+1 loops (DP-30), and the consult autosave debounce (idle 3 s / max 30 s, audit only sign/amend; DP-27) which removes most audited writes behind the chain lock. Unblocks doctor (autosave no longer contends), patient app (Phase 3 delta sync) and every SSE consumer.

stories.context: ADR-04 class C and D: departments, workflow selections, charge catalogue (prices, never stock), note/Rx templates, WhatsApp templates, roles -> permissions and plan entitlements cached in Caffeine L1 (5 min, refresh at 2.5) and Valkey L2 (1 h) under versioned keys nabd:{region}:t:{tid}:cfg:{domain}:v{ver}. Invalidation is an INCR of the version key by the cache-invalidator consumer (so only after commit) plus a pub/sub 'inval' broadcast that evicts L1 on all instances. Stampede control: single-flight AsyncLoadingCache, soft/hard TTL with SET NX lock, +/-10% jitter, warm-up at clinic opening. PHI default-deny: a test enumerates forbidden data classes (allergies, active meds, pregnancy, stock at dispense, slot at booking, invoice totals, break-glass) and fails if any is cached.
acceptance: Given the owner changes a consultation price, when the change commits, then every Core instance serves the new price within 5 s (p99) and checkout uses the new price
Given 200 concurrent requests for a cold config key, when loaded, then exactly one DB load happens per instance (single-flight) and at most one across instances (NX lock)

Given CacheKeys, when any key is built for tenant data, then it contains the tenant id; a unit test fails on raw string key construction (ArchUnit forbids direct template calls outside core.shared.cache)

Given the PHI default-deny test, when it scans @Cacheable usages and cache registrations, then allergies, active medications, pregnancy status, stock at dispense, slot availability at booking, invoice totals and break-glass state are never cached
Given a race repopulates L2 with a pre-commit value, when the version is bumped, then the stale value is unreachable
nfr: Config read p99 < 1 ms on L1 hit
TTL jitter +/-10%
Cache values never in logs/metrics
tests: integration: two instances, invalidation within 5 s

stories.title: Staff screens receive queue, nursing and doctor-status changes over one SSE stream within 2 s
stories.story: As a receptionist I want the arrivals board to update by itself within 2 seconds when a doctor calls the next patient so that I never tell a patient the wrong thing.
stories.context: ADR-05: GET /v1/events?topics=queue,nursing,doctor-status served by core.realtime on async servlets with Java 21 virtual threads. The sse-fanout consumer and the ETA engine publish deltas on Valkey pub/sub channels t:{tid}:q:{doctor}:{date}; each Core pod subscribes only to channels of its connected tenants. Protocol: snapshot on connect, then {type, id, v} deltas, Last-Event-ID resume from a short per-tenant-day stream (2 h retention), 25 s heartbeat comment, server-side permission filter per topic (nursing topic needs nursing:view). Auth via the BFF session cookie (T-063). A synthetic probe writes a test event every minute in each cell and measures event-to-screen latency (SLO 95% < 2 s, 99% < 5 s). Unblocks FRD RCP-01, PAT-05, SYS-05 and founder brief B-34/B-85.

Given a connection drops and reconnects with Last-Event-ID within 2 h, when it resumes, then missed deltas are replayed in order; older than 2 h returns a fresh snapshot
Given an idle stream, when 25 s pass, then a heartbeat comment is sent so proxies keep it open
Given a receptionist without nursing:view, when they request topics=nursing, then that topic is omitted and the response header lists granted topics
Given 3,000 concurrent connections per region across 3 pods, when load-tested, then heap stays < 70% and delivery p95 < 2 s
Given deltas, when inspected, then they carry ids, status, token, stage and version only; names come from the batch read endpoint

stories.title: Audited writes never queue behind each other: audit chain head is indexed and load-verified

stories.context: DP-05: audit_log_chain() finds the previous hash with ORDER BY id DESC LIMIT 1 FOR UPDATE filtered only by RLS — 5,041 ms for a quiet tenant at 3M rows — and holds the lock until the business transaction commits, serialising every audited write within a tenant. Immediate fix: audit_log (tenant_id, id DESC) (in OPS-001, measured 0.20 ms). T-053 (Core Backend) rebuilds the chain with an audit_chain_heads row updated via UPDATE ... RETURNING, UTC hashing and nightly verify. This story verifies performance under load and, if contention remains above budget, implements DP-05's next step: insert unchained rows in the business transaction and have one per-region sealer chain them asynchronously within seconds (keeping verify_audit_chain semantics) — the same batch-sealing model DEC-22 recommends for phi_read_log.
